task:
You are an independent engineering manuscript editor evaluating anonymous revised prose in its full section context.
Do not guess the writer, effort level, guide, or chronology. Read only this packet. Do not browse, read other files, consult agents, or rewrite candidates.
The author's priority is useful new engineering explanation without unnecessary repetition of earlier context or of another sentence in the target. Judge meaning, not lexical overlap. Technical terms, necessary definitions, new qualifications and short connections may legitimately recur. Do not reward shorter prose when meaning is lost, or require a standalone recap.
The original is not a style gold standard. Some of its prose is intentionally the problematic target. Use required_meaning as the engineering preservation checklist; established_context identifies information already available. Equations are locked and identical across candidates.
For every candidate, assess:
- repeated_claims: each unnecessary repetition as an object with quote, earlier_location, why_unnecessary, severity ("minor" or "material"). Quote exact candidate wording and identify the earlier sentence in context or candidate. Split one claim only once.
- missing_or_changed_meaning: specific omitted new fact, lost qualification, unsupported addition, or ambiguous relation. Do not require reintroducing known motivation.
- language_defects: awkward terminology, unnatural sentence or comma crowding, with exact evidence.
- ready: true only if no material redundancy or meaning defect or material language defect remains; minor optional wording preferences do not fail.
- score: 0..2 for each of fidelity, necessary_content, contribution, flow, clarity. 2 meets requirement, 1 local defect, 0 substantial defect. A score cannot override a material defect.
Compare every requested pair by fewer meaningful repairs: preference must be the first candidate id, second candidate id, or "tie". Reason must quote concrete evidence. advantage must be "none", "small", or "material". A tie is welcome when differences are optional.
Keep judgments independent of score totals. Do not invent errors merely to distinguish candidates. Evaluate all candidates and all requested pairs. Return one valid JSON object with candidates (array of objects with id, repeated_claims, missing_or_changed_meaning, language_defects, ready, score), comparisons (array of objects with pair_id, preference, advantage, reason), and limits (string).

before.text: where  α is a degradation factor ranging from 1 for a healthy structure to 0 for a completely damaged structure, and ζ is the damping ratio. Note that the degradation factor relates specifically to the loss in stiffness. This simplified stiffness-degradation model is needed to obtain a theoretical formulation of the stability boundary. In practice, degradation may also change other properties, particularly damping. However, increased damping has been shown to improve RTHS stability [31]. Therefore, neglecting any additional damping introduced by degradation represents a conservative assumption with respect to this effect.

original_target.text: To address the nonlinear and time-varying nature of structural degradation, a short-window linear approximation is used to keep the analysis tractable and suitable for online evaluation. Although this method may not be accurate during brief intervals where properties change rapidly, it is typically accurate before and after such events, and during periods where degradation evolves slowly.

after.text: With the real-time hybrid simulation (RTHS) framework blocks defined, a vRTHS is performed to evaluate various stability indicators. This analysis considers a three-story reference building where a portion of the first story acts as the physical substructure represented by an SDOF frame. More details on this study are provided in section 6. The stability analysis begins by simulating a healthy structure (α=1) and then progressively reducing the degradation factor, α​, to simulate the accumulation of damage. The level of specimen degradation is increased in this way to allow the system to approach an instability and illustrate the target behavior.

required_meaning: Degradation is nonlinear and time varying. Short-window linear approximation keeps analysis tractable and suitable for online evaluation.
Approximation may be inaccurate during brief rapid property changes. It is typically accurate before/after those events and during slow degradation. No guarantee or new algorithm.
Repeating the word degradation is not a defect. Its nonlinear/time-varying character motivates a new approximation here; do not delete the explanation just because degradation was mentioned earlier.
established_context: Previous paragraph defines a stiffness-degradation factor and caveat about damping. Next paragraph starts the virtual simulation.
